item.title: Are future-telling SCP's too overused?: Re: Are future-telling SCP's too overused?
item.content:encoded:
We've certainly seen quite a few precognitive SCPs; SCP-089 was an early example with some subtly, and SCP-2003 is mostly just the concept played straight, and SCP-5560 which uses it for some character-building. We additionally have a lot of anomalies from the future, such as SCP-4998, which achieves the same effect.

Point is that if your idea is just "SCP where something bad is going to happen in the future", it will likely not stand out much. Execution is the name of the game, though, so if your idea is genuinely unique it'll be able to excel.

If you'd like other examples try searching for future, temporal, and predictive in the Tag Search and sort by rating.

item.title: MC&D Involvement in Coalition: Re: MC&D Involvement in Coalition
item.content:encoded:
Just to be clear, the entity broadcasting these shows is not the anomaly but the show itself.

Again, why does he/the agents/the show do this in the first place?

Please answer straightforwardly rather than redirecting to two other threads.

This way the group can gather information from these anomalous groups without being a super-powered god.

Given that these are completely unknown random individuals seemingly with no motive who just happen to be able to infiltrate major GoIs to the point where they can critique them in a broadcast… you're probably going to get people calling this overpowered regardless of how many agents they've got. The best way to address this would be to drastically lower the number of GoIs that the broadcast is critiquing.

item.title: MC&D Involvement in Coalition: Re: MC&D Involvement in Coalition
item.content:encoded:
Just to be clear, the entity broadcasting these shows is not the anomaly but the show itself. It cannot be because I don't intend to reveal him in my article. However, for the sake of writing, I do feel that this character should be fleshed out even if he never appears. So how about this, the broadcaster is not a single person but a web of agents in these organizations who want to help improve their individual corporations. This way the group can gather information from these anomalous groups without being a super-powered god.
If you want a more solid idea on what I'm trying to accomplish here are links to my Idea Critiques:
http://www.scpwiki.com/forum/t-13137035/welcome-to-anomalous-analyticals
http://www.scpwiki.com/forum/t-13206177/welcome-to-anomalous-analyticals-x2

item.title: MC&D Involvement in Coalition: Re: MC&D Involvement in Coalition
item.content:encoded:
The broadcaster seems to want to help improve the organizations by critiquing them

If he's some generic overpowered "ethereal presence", and also a literal god, why does he have specific interest in this small niche of organizations compared to literally any other population of large corporations in the world?

This was meant to he a humorous article so feel free to give recommendations on improvements.

You're definitely going to need to make the motives more clear and relatable so the guy feels like a believable character and not just a plot device for making GoIs angry. Also, I feel like you're going to need to tone down how overpowered and untouchable the guy is, since "my super powerful OC gives hot takes on your favorite GoIs and no one can stop him" is probably not going to read as humor so much as an authorial power trip.

item.title: MC&D Involvement in Coalition: Re: MC&D Involvement in Coalition
item.content:encoded: The broadcaster seems to want to help improve the organizations by critiquing them, kinda like that one annoying person who doesn't quite know how to help you so points out everything you do wrong. I never actually plan for the coalition to capture him so for now I imagine him as some ethereal presence that can gather information to write these shows on without being threatened. Like a highly annoying god. This was meant to he a humorous article so feel free to give recommendations on improvements.

item.title: MC&D Involvement in Coalition: Re: MC&D Involvement in Coalition
item.content:encoded:
Would this be realistic?

I'm admittedly unsure, since MC&D tends to focus on exclusive items for a very select clientele. That makes this bit:

MC&D because they sell anomalous objects and such to customers. If this continued and their customers got wind of it they would find that anomalous objects such as the ones MC&D sell can be found outside their business

break my suspension of disbelief a bit as a reader since the anomalies MC&D offers to its clients and patrons wouldn't really be things that many other companies would be able to obtain.

could I get some suggestions on more realistic reasons for joining this coalition or other GOIs that might get involved?

I personally have a really hard time taking the "mysterious broadcaster" seriously. It seems really overpowered that they have so much information to start reviewing anomalous community organizations that also just happen to be prominent enough for the Foundation to notice them.

I feel like you'd need to first flesh out the random broadcaster more before thinking about the GoI reaction. What are the broadcaster's motives? What do they hope to accomplish with their reviews? If they know enough to write reviews, surely they know messing with those big-name GoIs could potentially threaten their own safety?

item.title: MC&D Involvement in Coalition: MC&D Involvement in Coalition
item.content:encoded:
Just a quick summary of my article for background information: A mysterious broadcaster has been analyzing and reviewing different anomalous organizations. This posed a threat to the anomalous society when a brief episode was broadcast in times square. The show eventually pissed off several organizations to the point where a few form a temporary coalition aimed at stopping these broadcasts.
The actual question: In this coalition, I included MC&D because they sell anomalous objects and such to customers. If this continued and their customers got wind of it they would find that anomalous objects such as the ones MC&D sell can be found outside their business which could lead to competition in their area. Would this be realistic? If not could I get some suggestions on more realistic reasons for joining this coalition or other GOIs that might get involved?

item.title: How do I use custom pictures in A.C.S: Re: How do I use custom pictures in A.C.S
item.content:encoded:
That's because you're not linking to an image, you're linking to a webpage which hosts the image for you. The raw image link is here: https://i.ibb.co/q987gKc/Omnia.png (usually indicated by the ".png", ".jpg", etc. at the end of the link)

Notably, Wikidot does allow for file hosting and it's highly recommended you take advantage of that instead of hosting on imgbb.com. You can save a file to your page via the Files button at the bottom and find the image url by clicking the filename once it's uploaded. This gives you the power as the uploader to determine if the file gets removed, as opposed to imgbb.com, and generally works with the best practice of reducing hotlinking from offsite to a minimum.

item.title: Use Of Another Author's/Existing Characters: Re: Use Of Another Author's/Existing Characters
item.content:encoded:
There is no policy against using the characters, concepts, storylines, etc. of others in your own article. Such a policy would run counter to the whole collaborative thing we're doing here.

The only sort of expectation for you if you're using Glass' characters is that you understand the character — make sure to represent him generally how he exists in other tales, to demonstrate a level of respect for the work others have put into him. The Tag Search can be helpful in this regard if you want to search his name and sort by highly rated.
